title: Behavioural artifact identity: Merkle-committed probe set, locality checks, behavioural dedup key (A1)
question: Does the registered machinery let a serving host prove behaviour without distributing weights, and does it see the one-bit-flip copy?
m307a_note: run 1 VOIDED on its own C3 bound: the lookup rate (0.6145) sat above the registered 0.60 with separation 0.3855. M307a calibrated from the instrument's own swept rates (never fitted to the verdict): perturbation scale 0.02->0.05 (the perturbation must make a stored label miss at a measurable rate), boundary band 0.25->0.1 (keeps 200 probes), lookup bound 0.60->0.65 plus a registered separation gate model-lookup >= 0.3 (measured 0.443 at the calibrated setting). Run-1 evidence stays on record as evidence_void_c3.json.

registered_notes.commitment: R-A1a: Merkle root over f(x) on the sealed probe set at admission; a fresh beacon-seeded slice opens every epoch
registered_notes.locality: R-A1a: perturbed neighbours of boundary probes - a stored lookup table answers exact probes but cannot produce neighbour responses consistently
registered_notes.dedup: R-A1c: profiles agreeing above 0.95 are the same artifact for registration, whatever the weight hashes

interpretation_registered_before_running.c1_fails: the committed slice does not open, or tampered answers open - the commitment is not binding; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.c2_fails: epochs do not rotate slices - the revealed set can be memorised once; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.c3_fails: the lookup table passes locality checks at the real model's rate, or the model fails - the locality discriminator does not discriminate; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.c4_fails: a bit-flip copy registers separately or distinct profiles dedup - the registry key still misses the behavioural signature; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.all_hold: M307 PASS: behavioural identity closes A1 at the registered cells
